articles.title: Severely disabled young people should get fast-track access to benefits, Milburn says
articles.summary:
Alan Milburn said 16- to 24-year-olds with most complex needs should not have to keep proving they cannot work

Young people whose complex disabilities mean they have little prospect of…

blocks.text: Young people whose complex disabilities mean they have little prospect of getting a paid job should get fast-track access to disability benefits, an official review of youth employment will say.

The review, by the former Labour health secretary Alan Milburn, will say 16- to 24-year-olds with the most severe lifelong needs should be guaranteed swift and unconditional benefit support rather than having to prove they cannot work.

Currently, many disabled youngsters and their families have to endure repeated lengthy, adversarial and often distressing assessments to access personal independence payment (Pip) and universal credit health benefits.

The guarantee could include young people with profound and multiple learning disabilities, severe neurological conditions, and those with severe and complex needs who qualify for NHS continuing healthcare support.

The review, expected in October, will say there is no need for repeated disability benefits assessments for this group, and young adults should not have to constantly demonstrate proof of lifelong conditions and impairments diagnosed at birth or in early childhood that mean they cannot work.

“I’ve heard too many stories of young people with the most severe disabilities left waiting, worrying and fighting for the support they’re entitled to,” Milburn told the Guardian. “Too often they’re having to battle through dehumanising tick-box assessments designed to catch people out, not care for them.”

He added: “A different approach is needed for disabled people whose condition is so severe that they could never work. By right they should get faster support rather than having to prove it over and over again to get the help they deserve.”

The separate government-commissioned Timms review into Pip concluded in an interim report earlier this year that the Pip assessment process was justifiably regarded by many claimants as “soul-destroying” and degrading.

The disability charity Sense, which supports disabled people with complex needs, welcomed the principle of fast-track guarantees but said it was important young people who were able and willing to work were not written off.

Harriet Edwards, the director of influencing at Sense, said: “It would be a significant step forward for young disabled people with the most complex needs and their families, and for those who have long campaigned to end the exhausting and humiliating process of multiple assessments.

“But we must not write young disabled people off. Those who want to and are able to work need specialist employment support and genuine opportunities, alongside the financial protection they need to live their lives.

“Government must now take this recommendation forward. The detail will be crucial, including who is eligible, whether exemptions go far enough, and how this will work across different disability benefits so people aren’t left navigating different rules and assessments.”

Tara Harris, 57, from the West Midlands, described obtaining disability benefits for her son Ollie, 25, who has complex disabilities, as a “bureaucratic nightmare”. She said the system involved “constant battles of chasing things and not having things. It’s ‘computer says no.’” It was also stressful. “I feel like I’ve had to be a tiger mum,” she said.

Harris said her son could not do paid work but had been supported to volunteer at a cafe two days a week. The Pip assessment required her to describe his progress in a routinely negative way. She fears that if she were to “put things in a positive language, then you don’t get Pip”.

She said: “It’s really hard to have these sorts of conversations in front of Oliver. Because it sort of demeans him, and he’s absolutely wonderful, amazing person and deserves to have money to be able to be an adult.”
The government commissioned Milburn to address a growing youth jobs crisis in the UK in which nearly 1 million 16- to 24-year-olds are classified as Neet (not in employment, education or training).

His interim report, published in June, made it clear young people diagnosed with lifelong complex needs who are never be able to work must be protected by the benefit system. But it also hinted that young people with less severe conditions who could be supported to work may see reductions in benefits

Milburn, a minister in Tony Blair’s government, last month called for investment in specialist internships designed to secure work for young people with special educational needs to address “devastating” joblessness rates for those with learning disability, autism and mental illness.

articles.title: Three-quarters of UK’s popular plug-in hybrid cars unable to use rapid chargers
articles.summary:
Only 26% of PHEVs sold across top 20 models can use chargers with power of 50kW or more, analysis finds

Three-quarters of the 20 top-selling plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) in the…

blocks.text: Three-quarters of the 20 top-selling plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) in the UK cannot use rapid chargers, research has found, amid concerns that many are essentially “petrol cars pulling round a heavy battery”.

The cars, which can run on electric batteries as well as combustion engines, have been promoted by carmakers as a way to cover long distances in a single drive – unlike fully electric cars – while still reducing emissions.

But only 26% of the vehicles sold across the top 20 models, which include the Jaecoo 7, the Ford Kuga and Hyundai Tucson, are able to use rapid chargers with powers of 50kW or more, according to analysis by the industry body, ChargeUK.

These chargers can quickly top up a car battery – for example at a motorway service station – adding a significant amount of range in 20 to 30 minutes. Cars that cannot use them are limited to much slower charging speeds, meaning drivers wanting to recharge mid-trip may face a wait of several hours. Hybrid owners may instead choose to rely on their petrol engines.

Shane Brennan, the chief executive of ChargeUK, said: “A plug-in hybrid electric vehicle that is never plugged in is a costly petrol car pulling round a heavy battery. PHEV drivers unable to charge on the public charging network quickly fall into patterns of being petrol reliant.

“Government must not be hoodwinked into promoting the idea that boosting PHEV sales is a meaningful step towards electrification. It is a spectacular own goal to be seduced by a mythical ‘PHEV compromise’.”

Repeated studies have found PHEVs pump out significantly more planet-heating pollution than official figures show. Despite this, the government last year allowed manufacturers to sell more of them towards their EV targets.
PHEVs were the fastest-growing type of car sold in the UK last year, with 227,000 registered – up almost 35% on 2024 – according to official data. A further 180,000 have been sold so far this year.
The top 20 models sold also include the BYD Seal, the MG HS and the BMW 3 Series, none of which can use rapid chargers.

In a recent consultation on the zero emission vehicle mandate, the government said PHEVs were driven on electric power far less than official figures suggested. The report said the method used to calculate emissions savings “significantly overestimates electric driving, as in real life many drivers charge infrequently, meaning real world CO2 emissions are higher than official figures”.

However, it is expected to weaken targets for pure EV sales even further when a consultation on changing the mandate closes in October, after a period of intense lobbying from the car industry. Last week, Nissan suggested it could withhold a £170m investment in its factory in Sunderland if the UK does not weaken the rules.

None of the top 20 models can use ultra-rapid chargers, the fastest tier on the network, capable of adding significant range in a matter of minutes. Rapid charging is defined as 50kW and above and ultra-rapid as from 150kW.
after newsletter promotion

Rapid and ultra-rapid chargers make up about a quarter of the UK’s public charging points, according to government figures, but deliver the majority of the network’s total charging capacity because they are so much faster.
By contrast, every one of the top 20 models of pure electric vehicles sold last year could use rapid chargers, and 64% could use ultra-rapid ones.
It comes after carmakers raised discounts on combustion engine cars last month, including hybrids, and weakened them on electric, as they neared their annual EV sales targets.

Autotrader said average discounts for petrol cars listed on its platform jumped sharply to 11.9% in September from 11.3% in August. Meanwhile EV discounts fell to 10.7% from 11.1%, which the group said was mainly down to companies such as Mercedes-Benz and MG “scaling back their incentives as they close in on their required ZEV mandate levels for the year”.

A government spokesperson said it was taking a practical approach by letting drivers choose plug-in hybrids, adding that the vehicles’ real-word carbon emissions were still 40% lower than the average petrol or diesel car.

articles.title: Record-breaking Albert Ian delos Santos earns Asian Games bronze
articles.summary: Filipino weightlifter Albert Ian delos Santos shatters his junior world and junior continental records on the way to an Asian Games bronze medal

blocks.text: POWER. Weightlifter Albert Ian delos Santos in action for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
Filipino weightlifter Albert Ian delos Santos shatters his junior world and junior continental records on the way to an Asian Games bronze medal
MANILA, Philippines – Young weightlifter Albert Ian delos Santos has made a habit of breaking records.
And he did so again in the 2026 Asian Games on the way to the bronze medal in the men’s 70kg division at the Nagoya City Trade and Industry Center in Japan on Saturday, September 26.

The youngest in the final at 20 years old, the Zamboangueño showed he can hold his own against the best in the continent as he shattered his own junior world and junior Asian marks in clean and jerk (183kg) and total lift (324kg) to earn his place on the podium.

Delos Santos ran fourth after the snatch portion with a clearance of 141kg but overtook Uzbekistan’s Adkhamjon Ergashev for the bronze by eclipsing his previous junior world and junior continental records in clean and jerk (180kg) and total lift (321kg), which he established in the Asian Youth and Junior Weightlifting Championships in August.
North Korea’s Ri Won Ju claimed the gold with hardly any resistance with 349kg, while Japan’s Masanori Miyamoto bagged the silver with 342kg.
Ergashev managed just 318kg and settled for fourth.
Delos Santos broke through for the Philippine weightlifting team after Rosegie Ramos and Elreen Ando fell short of medals.
Ramos finished fourth in the women’s 53kg class, while Ando placed fifth in the women’s 61kg division. – Rappler.com

articles.summary: Senator Panfilo "Ping" Lacson expressed his sympathies to the site engineers of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), saying agency chief Vince Dizon seemingly contradicted their…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 4:02pm

Senator Panfilo "Ping" Lacson expressed his sympathies to the site engineers of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), saying agency chief Vince Dizon seemingly contradicted their findings.

During the Senate hearing on the DPWH 2027 proposed budget, Senator Alan Peter Cayetano—who has been on verbal squabble with Lacson—asked Dizon if his political bailiwick of Taguig City had any ghost or non-existent infrastructure projects. Dizon said no ghost projects have been found in Taguig City so far, based on the department's current investigation.
In a statement on Saturday, Lacson said Dizon was suffering from a "clouded" memory.

"Poor DPWH Site Inspection Engineers. Their boss, Sec. Vince Dizon directly contradicted their own site inspection reports in Taguig, specifically submitted by personnel from the department's Bureau of Quality and Safety and Bureau of Maintenance," Lacson said in an X post.

In a separate post, Lacson said, "Poor Vince Dizon. The 'pressure' of work may have clouded his memory. The DPWH already turned over to my Senate office records of nonexistent but reported as completed slope protection projects in Taguig. Like toothpaste squeezed from the tube, there's no putting it back in," the senator said in a separate post.
GMA News Online has reached out to Dizon for a statement and will update the story once he responds.

According to Lacson, when Dizon said there were no ghost projects, it was inconsistent with site inspection reports of the DPWH's Bureaus of Maintenance, Quality and Safety, Construction, and Research and Standards.
Lacson said the reports found that there were several Taguig flood control projects that were declared as completed, and yet the inspection team could not validate their physical presence.
The senator also cited data from the DPWH's "Analysis of Potential Similar Billing Photographs from 2017-2025 of Taguig projects using AI-Based Image Similarity Detection Approach."
A billing photo is used to indicate the progress of a project.

He said 1,079 pairs of images out of 15,523 were flagged for high visual similarity. The report supposedly tagged 180 unique contracts with 10 contractors with the most number of projects with similar billing photos.

Alleged similar billing photos were found in 16 unique projects of one contractor; 10 or more projects involving five firms; and at least five similar photos across all 10 contractors. — VDV, GMA News
