blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 12:37pm

The National Citizens' Movement for Free Elections (NAMFREL) on Saturday expressed dismay over the postponement of the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) and said that it will support and join efforts to question its constitutionality.
This comes after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed the postponement into a law on Friday.

"The law was made public only on September 25, mere days before the scheduled filing of certificates of candidacy on September 28. NAMFREL had, on two separate occasions this year — April 17 and August 5, 2026 — publicly and unequivocally called on Congress and the Executive to reject exactly this outcome," NAMFREL said in a statement.
"That these repeated warnings went unheeded is deeply troubling. That the law was rushed to enactment just ahead of the filing period is more troubling still," it added.
EXPLAINER: What to know about the new law moving the BSKE to 2028?

Marcos said Friday that the postponement will allow officials to use the postponement "to further improve service delivery, complete programs that have already been initiated, and focus more intently on the needs of every community, family, and the youth."
NAMFREL, however, said that it "respectfully but firmly rejects this reasoning."

"A government genuinely intent on addressing the crises it cites — fiscal pressure, the need for efficient and accountable frontline service delivery — should be seeking a renewed and fresh mandate for barangay leadership, not extending the tenure of officials without a single vote cast in their favor," NAMFREL said.

"NAMFREL's position on this point has not changed: economic hardship is, if anything, all the more reason to ensure accountable, freshly-mandated leadership at the level of government closest to the people — not less," it added.
Supreme Court
The election watchdog also emphasized that the postponement resulted in "wasted funds" amid its preparations for the polls, which has now been moved to 2028.

"Barangay and SK elections are already the most frequently postponed democratic exercises in the country's history. Each additional deferral normalizes the practice of legislating around the electorate rather than submitting to it, and makes the next postponement easier to justify," NAMFREL said.

"NAMFREL will support and join the effort of individuals and groups moving to question the constitutionality of RA 12326. Election watchdog groups have expressed its intent to bring the matter before the Supreme Court, and election lawyers have likewise announced the filing of a Petition for Certiorari, arguing that the law “strikes at the heart of our democracy and reflects a grave abuse of discretion.”
The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has said that it is expecting the filing of petitions before the Supreme Court (SC) challenging the the postponement of the BSKE.

“Ang problem po talaga namin ay paano nga kung may pumunta sa Korte Suprema at magkaroon ng tinatawag na injunctive restraining order,” Comelec Chairman George Garcia told Super Radyo dzBB in an interview.
(Our problem is what if someone goes to the Supreme Court and gets an injunctive restraining order.)
In a separate interview on Super Radyo dzBB, election lawyer Romulo Macalintal said he will file a petition questioning the postponement of the BSKE on Monday.

Macalintal said his camp is preparing the petition that will be filed with the SC, arguing that the postponement would result in an unreasonable extension of the terms of incumbent barangay and SK officials.
“Kapag natuloy ito, tatlong taon na postponement. Tatlong taon na extended ang term nila,” he said.
(If the postponement happens, it will be a three-year postponement. Their term will be extended by three years.) —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: OpenAI works to understand full scope of agent activity as user data leak emerges
articles.summary: OpenAI grapples with rogue agent incidents as privacy risks mount, revealing challenges in controlling AI behavior and prompting calls for industry caution.

blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO/WASHINGTON, US – Two months after OpenAI disclosed the accidental hacking of Hugging Face, the ChatGPT maker is still working to understand the full scope of its rogue agent activity, two people briefed on the matter told Reuters.

The latest example came on Friday when OpenAI said its agents had leaked 53 images from ChatGPT users. OpenAI declined to say if the images were AI-generated or identified real people. It also declined to say when the images were posted.

The disclosure and researcher reports on Friday of other previously unknown activity involving several US agencies reveal a new area of privacy risk for the company, and illustrate how difficult it is even for an AI firm at the cutting edge of the technology to inventory all the unauthorized activity tied to its agents. OpenAI’s ongoing battle also reflects a yawning gap between the strength of the models the company is testing and its capacity to oversee or even track their actions.

As of mid-September, one person briefed on the matter estimated that OpenAI had found roughly two dozen incidents of its agents acting in undesirable ways. But the number has continued rising as OpenAI teams sift through internal logs of the agents’ activities and find previously unknown cases, the two people close to the company said.
OpenAI said its review would take months to complete given the scale of the work.
The company also said it had notified dozens of third parties about improper activity.
Most of the leaked images have been taken down and OpenAI said it was lobbying hosting providers to remove the rest.

OpenAI’s agents had access to these images because the company relies on anonymized user data for part of its model-training process, according to the company, former employees and outside researchers. Enterprise data is not eligible for training, while ChatGPT consumers need to opt out of allowing the company to use their data for training.

Before user posts are used for training, they go through an anonymization process that strips out metadata, names and other contact information and should make it difficult to trace back to any individual user, the company said.

But the practice carries risks because there is a chance that the data may not be fully stripped of personally identifiable information and that it might leak in the course of the model’s work, three people familiar with OpenAI’s practices said.

OpenAI said late on Friday its models accessed information from the websites of the US Securities and Exchange Commission and the US Census Bureau during research and training activity, but found no evidence of unauthorized access, compromised accounts or security breaches.
Separately, AI research nonprofit Transluce said agents appearing to originate from OpenAI made an unsuccessful attempt to hack a US Department of Education civil rights website.
Transluce said the incident was part of broader AI agent activity probing government websites using tactics including exposed credentials, anti-bot bypasses and fake accounts.

In the two months since OpenAI first announced that its agents broke containment, there have been more than 15 different OpenAI-related incidents of varying levels of severity disclosed by the company, by outside researchers, or — just on Wednesday — by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the United Nations, who said OpenAI agents broke into a government health data portal in June.

Past incidents have varied in nature, ranging from spam-like messages left on internet sites all the way to the break-in at Hugging Face, which involved a swarm of agents abusing previously unknown software vulnerabilities to escape their networks and penetrate the AI repository as they hunted for answers to a test. OpenAI also said its agents took aim at its own infrastructure.

Albanese told reporters in New York that OpenAI uncovered the activity in August, and disclosed it on September 10 via an email to a general government inbox. He said he directly told OpenAI CEO Sam Altman that this disclosure process was unacceptable.
OpenAI said some of the sites involved are operated by government, universities and public agencies because the models that are conducting research seek out reputable sources of public information.

The July 21 announcement that ​OpenAI’s agents had slipped out of control and hacked Hugging Face sparked widespread worries within the AI industry over its ability to control the more powerful AI models under development now. Since then, Anthropic, Alphabet’s Google and Meta have said they’ve found similar behavior by their agents after the Hugging Face incident prompted them to search.

OpenAI has acknowledged a general need for more transparency around rogue AI behavior. On September 16, the company published a new framework for disclosing such incidents, saying it would err on the side of transparency “even when significance is uncertain.”

Even so, two people familiar with OpenAI’s investigation into its agents’ activity described it as locked down and shaped by company lawyers. The process has been unusually compartmentalized for a company that some former employees say was more open about these issues in the past, the people said.
Roughly 100 people were in some way involved in the process to understand the Hugging Face hack, three people briefed on the matter said. During that process, evidence of other incidents surfaced.

Reuters has previously reported that OpenAI investigators looking into the Hugging Face breach were discouraged by the company’s lawyers from expanding the scope of the investigation to include other incidents. OpenAI said its lawyers did not discourage deeper investigation.
Many incidents have been uncovered by outside researchers rather than OpenAI directly. In several episodes, the agents took problematic actions that went unnoticed by the company for months.

Earlier this month, a small group of investigators discovered that the company’s agents had hijacked a mostly defunct German wiki site to share tactics to cheat on some tasks, bypass OpenAI’s restrictions and mask their behavior.

This week, the AI research firm Transluce said it discovered that OpenAI agents had bypassed the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare’s anti-bot controls. The firm also found two other cases that it linked to OpenAI agents. Those incidents were separate from the activity disclosed by Albanese.

In a statement, OpenAI said “much of the activity described in Transluce’s report overlaps with cases at varying stages of investigation in our ongoing review of misaligned model activity.” The company said it is prioritizing the most severe cases in its review.

Since the Hugging Face hack, researchers across the AI industry have grown worried that companies will not be able to predict or control their technology. Some have taken the path of former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who publicly resigned this month in a viral social-media thread that said the AI labs are “gambling with our lives.”

In response to those concerns, Altman and his counterpart at Anthropic, CEO Dario Amodei, called for the industry to “pace” the development of AI and move cautiously in its pursuit of “recursive self improvement.” Altman doubled down on that message this week while addressing the United Nations.
Even so, both companies rolled out new models on Tuesday. – Rappler.com

articles.title: TikTok to pay Alabama $100m and limit teenage use in first state settlement
articles.summary:
Trial had been set for Monday over claims by Alabama that TikTok misled parents about tools meant to shield children from harmful content

TikTok has agreed to pay Alabama at least $100m and…

blocks.text: TikTok has agreed to pay Alabama at least $100m and enact time limits and other restrictions for teenage users, avoiding a trial with a settlement that was modelled on Instagram-owner Meta’s recent agreement with US states.
Alabama described it as a “first-in-the-nation settlement” with a state in the sweeping litigation over social media’s affect on teen wellbeing.
A trial had been set to begin on Monday in the southern US state over claims by Alabama that TikTok misled parents about tools meant to shield children from harmful content.

TikTok’s settlement with Alabama mirrors safety provisions agreed by Meta, including a two-hour daily time limit for teens, restricted access from midnight to 6am, and suspending notifications during school hours.
It will also strengthen age verification, ban beauty filters for teenagers, and offer young users a non-personalised content feed.

Attorney general Steve Marshall hailed Friday’s settlement as “a great day for Alabama parents”. He said: “Tonight, they can rest easier knowing real protections are in place to shield their children from the dangers of social media addiction.”

Under the settlement, TikTok will send $100m to Alabama and could possibly pay up to $300m in total if 40 other attorneys general sign similar agreements with the company within a specified timeframe.
Alabama’s suit was the latest in a wave of litigation targeting social media companies across the United States about alleged harm their apps cause young users.
In August, Meta agreed to pay $18bn to settle a sweeping lawsuit brought by US states accusing it of designing Instagram and Facebook to get children addicted.
In addition, the Alabama deal includes a conditional restriction that Meta also agreed to: expanding the night-time shutdown period to 10pm to 7am if other platforms also commit to do the same.
“TikTok’s priority has always been fostering a safe and positive space where people can be creative, discover what they love, and connect with their community,” a company spokesperson told AFP.
“This builds on our commitment and core objective to continually enhance our robust safety tools to protect teens,” the spokesperson added.
More than a dozen other states, including California and New York, still havesuits against TikTok.
The company has previously settled cases against it that were headed for trial, including a Los Angeles lawsuit brought by a young woman and a suit from a Kentucky school district.
Meta, by contrast, has taken its chances in court – with bruising results.
In March, a jury in New Mexico ordered the Facebook and Instagram owner to pay $375m after finding it had misled the public about the safety of its platforms for children.
That same month, a Los Angeles jury found Meta and Google’s YouTube negligent in the case of a 20-year-old woman who said she became hooked on social media as a child, awarding her $6m.
Going to trial would have exposed TikTok to unprecedented public scrutiny of how it handles safety, with company documents and executive testimony potentially aired in open court.
Alabama originally sued TikTok and its Chinese parent company ByteDance in April 2025, alleging the app was engineered to hook young users “just like a sophisticated gambling machine”.

The state later narrowed its case to claims under Alabama’s Deceptive Trade Practices Act, focusing on whether TikTok misrepresented the effectiveness of features such as “Restricted Mode” and “Kids Mode.”

The lawsuit accused TikTok of falsely claiming it limits access to sexual and violent content for young users to have its app rated safe for teens in app stores run by Google, Apple and Microsoft and of misleading users about the Chinese government’s access ‌to US users’ data.

TikTok said it designed its platform with teen safety as a key priority and argued that section 230 of the federal Communications Decency Act shields online platforms from liability for user-generated content.
With Agence France-Presse and Reuters

articles.title: It’s an ADMM-Plus joint sail, but where were the Southeast Asians?
articles.summary: In an Philippine and Japan-hosted and ASEAN-led joint sail, most Southeast Asian navies were absent. So was China.

blocks.text: It was a breathtaking sight to see — 10 gray ships, sailing alongside each other — as the Philippines’ flagship, the BRP Jose Rizal, led the way.

Fine weather, for the most part, graced the two-day maritime activity under the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM)-Plus and its Experts’ Working Groups (EWGs) as navies of Southeast Asia and their partners practiced how they could help each other out in case of emergency in the South China Sea.
The partners showed up big time.

India and New Zealand sent two vessels each, including Wellington’s resupply vessel, the HMNZS Aotearoa. Japan’s JS Ise, a helicopter destroyer, was a domineering presence in the lineup. Australia and the US also sent a warship each.
Singapore sent the RSS Justice while Brunei sent the KDB Darussalam, although it would later bow out of the seaphase activity.

blocks.caption: It’s an ADMM-Plus joint sail, but where were the Southeast Asians?

blocks.text: Manila’s BRP Tarlac, the first landing platform dock to be delivered under the revised modernization program of 2012, joined the Rizal as well.
So where was the rest of the Philippines’ SEAblings — or fellow members of ASEAN? And where was China, a dialogue partner to both ASEAN and ADMM-Plus?

Where the exercise took place could offer a clue — waters between Zambales and Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal), a high-tide feature that’s within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone, claimed by several countries, and under China’s virtual control since 2012.

Bajo de Masinloc has been a flashpoint for tensions between Manila and Beijing for years — most notably in 2012, when the two countries had a tense standoff in the shoal. While Manila retreated under a truce the US had supposedly brokered, Beijing did not.
At least one China Coast Guard vessel and several of its auxiliary Chinese Maritime Militia stand guard at the shoal’s sole entrance at all times.

That 2012 standoff is what spurred the 2012 Revised Armed Forces of the Philippines Modernization law. It’s also what pushed Manila to bring Beijing to court, and eventually win the landmark 2016 Arbitral Award — the same award China does not recognize.
But back to the ADMM-Plus drill.

blocks.caption: ADMM-PLUS SAIL. The BRP Jose Rizal leads 10 other warships during a division tactics drill in the West Philippine Sea on September 23, 2026.

blocks.text: It wouldn’t be a stretch to think that Beijing, since it claims sovereignty over and has control of, Bajo de Masinloc, would want to boycott any joint drill near it. It wouldn’t be surprising if China convinced — or pressured — other ASEAN countries to opt out of the drill, too.
Talk is, both things happened.
ASEAN members, however, were in full attendance in the land-based events, including in subject matter expert exchanges and even a Future Leaders’ Program.

China’s ties with the 11 members of ASEAN vary dramatically. Most surveys indicate that the Philippines tends to be an outlier in the region when it comes to its perception of China, mostly because of West Philippine Sea issues.

In a lengthy statement, the Philippines’ Department of National Defense said it remains committed to the “principles, purpose, and objectives” of ADMM and its EWG as it “[provides] important platforms for practical cooperation, camaraderie, confidence-building, and mutual understanding among participating countries in addressing contemporary security challenges.”

The DND, whose head, Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. is also chair of ADMM, said the joint sail’s location was done by the book — through the usual ADMM-Plus processes and “based on operational, logistical, and other practical considerations discussed during the Initial Planning Conference (IPC) in March 2025 and subsequent planning conferences, which was attended by all participating countries, including China.”

It went on: “The designated exercise location, which is near Bajo de Masinloc (BdM), has long served as a venue for the Philippines’ bilateral and multilateral maritime exercises, including the ASEAN Multilateral Naval Exercise (AMNEX) held in 2023. This is in consideration of the area’s proximity to the Philippines’ largest naval port facility, which ensures that the necessary infrastructure and logistical support to accommodate the widest possible participation are met, including adequate berthing facilities, sustainment services, and operational support for participating naval assets.”

By largest naval port facility, the DND was referring to Naval Operating Base in Subic, where most of the Philippine Navy’s newest warships are usually berthed. The day before the exercise, warhips of India, Singapore and Brunei were all docked at the same base.
The DND also clarified the Philippines’ position on Bajo de Masinloc as an “integral and longstanding part of the Philippine national territory.”

As a high-tide elevation, Bajo de Masinloc generates its own 12 nautical-mile territorial sea. Its classification as a high-tide elevation also means the arbitral tribunal could not rule on who had sovereignty over it, since that was beyond its jurisdiction.

blocks.caption: It’s an ADMM-Plus joint sail, but where were the Southeast Asians?

blocks.text: The tribunal did, however, say that since the shoal was the traditional fishing ground of Filipino, Vietnamese, Chinese, and Taiwanese fisherfolk, they should not be hindered from access to it. Beijing has routinely driven away Filipino fisherfolk who try to sail close to the shoal’s once plentiful waters.

Bilateral ties between the Philippines and China have vascilated between tense and strained in the recent years under Marcos, primarily over disputes in an area of the South China Sea that Manila calls the West Philippine Sea.
Tensions have eased considerably beginning 2026, as Marcos sought a “reset” and Manila assumed chairship of ASEAN.

But that reset is backdropped by a strong pushback against China, over its supposed untrustworthiness as a negotiator — chief of those critics being Teodoro, who chairs ADMM. The Philippine defense chief has also been sanctioned by Beijing for his remarks.
So what happens when he hosts defense ministers from ASEAN and its partners — including China — before 2026 ends? – Rappler.com

articles.title: White House bars CNN from covering upcoming Trump trip, broadcaster says
articles.summary: CNN said its journalists have been barred from accompanying President Donald Trump on his upcoming trip to Tennessee. The episode marks the Trump administration's latest salvo against the major cable…

image.caption: Trump banned reporters from CNN from White House grounds earlier this week, with main networks having suspended coverage in solidarity as wellImage: Bonnie Cash/UPI Photo/Newscom/picture alliance

blocks.text: American news broadcaster CNN said its journalists were not allowed to board Air Force One for a planned trip with President Donald Trump on Saturday.
CNN was scheduled to travel on Air Force One to Knoxville, Tennessee, where Trump was expected to watch a college football game.

The news organization was to be the representative of the TV press pool for the weekend, meaning that it would cover the president and share video and information with the four other big networks that are part of the press pool.
CNN was replaced by Real America's Voice News, a conservative network, the Associated Press reported.
The episode represents the latest showdown between the Trump administration and media networks that the president believes to be unfavorable in their coverage.
Trump bans media outlets from White House
Trump bans CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from White House
Trump earlier this week barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House after he said the networks report "fiction and lies."
Major TV networks, including DW, then cut off their pooled coverage of the president in solidarity.
A federal judge temporarily struck down the ban in a ruling on Thursday after the outlets filed a lawsuit.
But the order from the judge addressed "hard passes" to the White House grounds and didn't directly address pool duties.

articles.title: P60 wage hike for Metro Manila minimum wage earners takes effect
articles.summary: Minimum wage earners in Metro Manila will get a P60 daily wage increase starting Saturday, September 26, under a new wage order issued by the Department of Labor and Employment.

blocks.text: September 26, 2026 | 11:46am
This undated photo shows an individual counting Philippine peso bills.
The Philippine STAR / Walter Bollozos

MANILA, Philippines — Minimum wage earners in Metro Manila will get a P60 daily wage increase starting Saturday, September 26, under a new wage order issued by the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE).
DOLE said all employers in the National Capital Region are required to comply with Wage Order No. NCR-28, which takes effect Saturday.
The order raises the daily minimum wage for nonagricultural workers from P695 to P755.
For agricultural workers, the minimum wage increases from P658 to P718 per day.
The P60 increase also covers workers in service and retail establishments with 15 or fewer workers and manufacturing establishments regularly employing fewer than 10 workers.
Wage Order No. NCR-28 was issued by the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board-National Capital Region after consultations among labor, employers and the government.
The new wage order comes as the previous NCR wage hike remains tied up in court.
Wage Order No. NCR-27 provided for a P85 increase in the NCR minimum wage in two tranches. The first P60 increase was supposed to take effect in July, followed by a P25 increase in January 2027.
Its implementation was halted after contractors Readycon Training & Construction Corp. and R-II Builders Corp. challenged the wage order in court.
A Pasig City court later issued an injunction blocking the implementation of NCR-27.
With NCR-28 now in effect, the NCR minimum wage for nonagricultural workers stands at P755 per day, while agricultural workers will receive P718.
DOLE said it will monitor compliance with the new wage rates.

articles.title: DOH on Code White due to Severe Tropical Storm Queenie
articles.summary: The Department of Health on Saturday raised a Code White Alert to ensure prompt response due to the possible effects of Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (international name: Surigae).

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 11:29am
The Department of Health (DOH) on Saturday raised a Code White Alert to ensure prompt response due to the possible effects of Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (international name: Surigae).
"Sa ilalim ng Code White Alert status, nakaalerto 24/7 ang DOH Operations Center para sa mabilis na pagtugon sa mga apektadong komunidad," the DOH said.
(Under a Code White Alert status, the DOH Operations Center in on alert 24/7 for immediate response to affected communities.)
Under Code White, health emergency teams, health commodities, and emergency rooms of DOH hospitals are on standby at all times to respond to road accidents, injuries, and health emergencies.
The DOH said it is continuing to coordinate with the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC), local government units, and regional disaster units due to Queenie.

Severe Tropical Storm Queenie, which is expected to intensify into a typhoon within the day, is not forecast to make landfall or have a direct effect on the country, PAGASA said in its 11 a.m. bulletin on Saturday.
However, Queenie will bring rains and possibly flooding, the DOH said.
The Health department then advised the public to avoid wading through floodwaters to prevent contracting leptospirosis and other diseases.
If one has no choice but wade through floodwaters, the DOH urges the public to consult the nearest health facility or YAKAP clinic for medical attention. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Brazil's Lula bans online gambling ahead of presidential election
articles.summary: Lula, who is currently in a tight presidential race against Flávio Bolsonaro, said the industry was a "cancer" that he must "remove".

blocks.text: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has announced a ban on online gambling, just days before an election in which he is seeking a fourth term as the country's leader.
Lula, who is running against the son of the incarcerated former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, signed a provisional order on Friday that "prohibits all sports betting and online casinos".
The online gambling industry in Brazil was legalised in 2018 and has since been blamed for widespread household income losses due to addiction.
Lula described the industry as a "cancer" in his announcement, adding "either we remove the tumour, or it kills us".
The move comes just over a week before the first round of voting in Brazil's presidential election. Recent polls have the 80-year-old leader almost neck-and-neck with Flávio Bolsonaro.
The new measures must receive congressional approval within 120 days to remain in force.
Lula acknowledged online betting was created under the former President Michel Temer's administration but that it "grew without regulation under Bolsonaro's management", in a statement on X .
He said that there were "no restrictions" particularly for preventing children and adolescents from accessing online betting.
"We won't allow betting companies to profit at the expense of Brazilian families' income and lives," the president added.
The president described how he had heard from families who had sold everything in their houses because of their gambling addictions.
Separate to the online betting order, Lula also signed a bill to penalise criminal offences related to fixed-odds betting.
Earlier this week, at the United Nations General Assembly, Lula accused the industry of "transforming addiction into profit".
But Flávio Bolsonaro called the gambling crackdown "populist, hypocritical and politically motivated" during a campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro on Friday, according to Reuters.
Most types of gambling, such as casinos and slot machines, are illegal in Brazil, but ever since online betting was legalised in 2018, it has exploded in popularity.
About 59.9% of Brazilian adults support banning internet betting, a survey by Atlas and Bloomberg published this week has found.

articles.title: CHED ready to issue policy on use of lived names by LGBTQIA+ students
articles.summary: The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) is ready to issue a policy recognizing the lived names or identities of students in the country's Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) who are transgender,…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 11:20am

The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) is ready to issue a policy recognizing the lived names or identities of students in the country's Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) who are transgender, queer, non-binary, or belong to other LGBTQIA+ sectors.

According to a report by Isa Avendaño-Umali on Super Radyo dzBB, the commission's stance on the matter was relayed by House Appropriations Vice Chair Monique Lagdameo of Makati City's First District, sponsor of the proposed CHED budget for 2027.

During budget deliberations Friday, Akbayan party-list Representative Perci Cendaña raised the topic on lived names, or identities used by an individual which may differ from how it is provided in one's birth certificate.
Cendaña cited the decision of state-run Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP) to allow students to be called by their lived names during its graduation ceremonies.
Lagdameo said CHED does not see any problem with this and remains open to engage in further discussions with stakeholders.
The report said one possible wrinkle, however, is with regard to the student's official records, since names are matched with entries from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA).
ALAMIN: Ano ang 'Sharmaine Bill' na kinikilala ang lived identities ng mga miyembro ng LGBTQ+ community?

Last June, Akbayan party-list filed House Bill 9929, or the Lived Identities Recognition Bill. It is otherwise known as the "Sharmaine Bill," in recognition of the viral orange fruit which sought to have its name changed to "Sharmaine."
The measure seeks to allow LGBTQIA+ members to use their lived names and simplify the process for this.
Its provisions provide the administrative mechanism for name change for those aged 18 years or older.

If enacted, the PSA will be tasked to enforce the change. Applicants will be allowed to secure a Certificate of Name Change or Gender Recognition, and an updated PSA birth certificate without any annotation about the name change. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Sara Duterte denies ex-Velasco aide’s claim he delivered over P2 billion to her
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte denied knowing Police Corporal Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. and receiving money from him, after the former security aide of ex-House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco alleged that he…

blocks.text: September 26, 2026 | 11:09am
Vice President Sara Duterte arrives at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court on Sept. 11, 2026 for the arraignment of the three counts of grave threats filed by the Department of Justice against her.
The Philippine STAR / Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte denied knowing Police Corporal Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. and receiving money from him, after the former security aide of ex-House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco alleged that he delivered more than P2 billion in cash to her.
“I do not know Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., nor have I ever received any money from him,” Duterte said in a statement posted on Facebook on September 26.

Gracioso, who claimed to have served as Velasco’s head of security from 2018 until the latter’s speakership from 2020 to 2022, alleged that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte and Davao City 1st District Rep. Paolo Duterte on Velasco’s instructions.

He estimated that he delivered more than P2 billion to the vice president on more than 20 occasions. His sworn affidavit, a copy of which the National Bureau of Investigation gave to GMA News, detailed alleged deliveries of P20 million to P50 million in cash to various locations in Metro Manila, Davao and other areas.
The NBI is investigating Gracioso’s claims. NBI Director Melvin Matibag said the agency conducted a polygraph test on Gracioso and validated some of his statements through other means.
Duterte said her lawyers are waiting for an official copy of Gracioso’s affidavit from the NBI so they can begin preparing cases against him.
“Once we are done dismantling the lies contained in his testimony, it will end up in the trash bin—just like the one from Ramil Madriaga,” she said.
Madriaga has previously been described by Gracioso as Duterte’s alleged bagman and aide, a connection Duterte has denied.
Duterte also described Gracioso’s allegations as “another media stunt” and an attempt to revive what she called a “faltering impeachment case.”
“This is nothing more than another media stunt, an attempt to breathe life into a faltering impeachment case,” Duterte said.
She accused the administration of seeking to bring her down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections and remain in power.
“The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical,” she said.
Duterte also called on President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to undergo a public drug test and answer for the flood control scandal, saying that Filipinos want change.
“The people want Marcos to take a public drug test. The people want Marcos to answer for the flood control scandal. The people want change,” she said.
“No amount of political maneuvering, propaganda, or manufactured distractions can ultimately silence the Filipino people,” Duterte added.

articles.title: TikTok agrees to settle with Alabama state over teen safety
articles.summary: The settlement involves TikTok adding several child safety measures to its platform including time limits and increased parental control. It is similar to a recent settlement competitor Meta had…

image.caption: TikTok has agreed to stricter access measures for teens, in what Alabama state has hailed as a 'landmark settlement'Image: Rüdiger Wölk/IMAGO

blocks.text: Short-form content sharing platform TikTok and its Chinese parent company ByteDance reached a settlement with Alabama, the southeastern US state said on Friday, days ahead of what would have been a revealing trial over teen safety and its impact on their mental health.

As part of the deal, TikTok agreed to pay $100 million (€87.7 million) to the state of Alabama and enact measures for teens including a two-hour daily use limit, restricted access for children and pauses after 15 minutes of use.
However, the payout could rise to $300 million if 40 other states sign similar agreements with the company within a stipulated time period, the document said.
What have TikTok and Alabama state said after the settlement?
"This builds on our commitment and core objective to continually ​enhance our robust safety tools to protect teens," a spokesperson for TikTok's US operations said in a statement.
Meta settles for $18B. What it means for you.
Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall sued the social media giant last year.

At least 27 other states and Washington DC have brought similar lawsuits. Apart from these, TikTok faces thousands of lawsuits by individuals, school districts and municipalities over its impact on teen mental health. Meta Platforms, Snap Inc and Alphabet's YouTube are also defendants in many of these ​cases.

"This is a great day for Alabama parents. Tonight, they can rest easier knowing real protections are in place to shield their children from the dangers of social media addiction. TikTok has agreed to give parents real control over what their kids see and how much time they spend on the app," Marshall said in a press release.
With this, the company has settled all cases selected for trial against it, including claims by five young people and a Kentucky school district.
What were the allegations against TikTok?

The state of Alabama had argued that TikTok's endless stream of videos makes it the most addictive of social media platforms and that its algorithm specifically pushes young users toward content about violence and self harm.
The state held the app partially responsible for a teen mental health crisis and a significant increase in emergency room visits.
The lawsuit also accused TikTok of falsely claiming that it limits access to sexual and violent content for young users to have the app rated as 'safe for teens' on app stores.
It said that TikTok asks users to self-report their ages but also allows them to evade questions by viewing videos without creating an account.
That still earns the company data on viewing habits. Being able to scroll videos without signing in makes 'Kids Mode' an entirely useless feature, the lawsuit said.
France debates social media ban for teenagers
What measures will TikTok take?
As per the settlement, TikTok has to implement a series of safety measures, including:

items: Two-hour daily limit
Additional parental control limiting time on platform
'Productive pauses' interrupting continuous scrolling after 15 minutes, 60 minutes and 90 minutes
Restrict children access from 12 a.m. to 6 a.m.
Restrictions on push notifications during night and school hours
Robust measures to verify user age
Limits on discoverability of teen accounts by adults
Sending parents notifications of suspicious interactions between teen users and adults
Blanket ban on use of cosmetic filters by teens
Non-personalized feed for teens

blocks.text: Last month, Meta agreed to pay a massive $17 billion to 47 US states and territories in a similar case while agreeing to make changes to teens' access to its platforms, Facebook and Instagram.
It did not admit wrongdoing and conditioned $5 billion of the payout on TikTok, Snap and YouTube's adoption of the same terms. TikTok has not commented publicly about that deal.

articles.title: Rodrigo Duterte defense team decries huge evidence, asks ICC to order a cap
articles.summary: The defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte has asked the International Criminal Court Trial Chamber to order the prosecution to limit the number of evidence in the case as this has…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 10:21am

The defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte has asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber to order the prosecution to limit the number of evidence in the case as this has ballooned by almost 1,000%.
Defense counsel Peter Haynes filed a motion on Friday, September 25, asking the Trial Chamber to limit the evidence to 10,000 items by October 7 at the latest.

"The Prosecution disclosed 5,275 items of evidence in the confirmation phase. Having heard the Trial Chamber’s request for a tight case record, it then chose to expand this to 62,130 items at the time of writing, being a 978% increase. The Prosecution’s 'massive' List of Evidence currently comprises 19,238 of those items. The Defence has no ability to read this volume of evidence prior to trial. However, even a cursory review demonstrates that much of the disclosed material is of extremely limited or no relevance to the charges in this case," Hanes said.

"The sheer volume of material, disclosed to the Defence three months before the start of trial, undermines Mr Duterte’s right to adequate time for the preparation of his defence pursuant to Article 67(1)(b). Even if the Prosecution were to condense its List of Evidence in advance of the next Status Conference, as suggested by the Chamber, the Defence must still review all 62,130 items disclosed to it, totalling over 320,000 pages of documents and 1,000 items of audio-visual material, in order to prepare for trial. On a conservative estimate of three minutes per page, it would take 16,000 person hours to review every disclosed item of documentary evidence just once," he added.
Haynes also said the quality of the added evidence is "abysmal."

"The Defence has raised systematic and persistent disclosure problems with the Prosecution. These include: tens of thousands of documents with incorrect descriptions, dates and other metadata; thousands of ‘floating’ pages that are detached from the remainder of the documents to which they belong; hundreds of illegible or blank items; thousands of duplicates or repetitive items; hundreds of untranslated and/or untranscribed audio and video files, and material disclosed in unreadable formats. Proceeding to trial on this basis would undermine the efficiency of proceedings and, by consequence, Mr Duterte’s right to trial without undue delay." he said.

"In ordinary circumstances, the obvious remedy would be to vacate the start date of trial to allow the Defence adequate time to review the full record of disclosure and prepare for trial. Herein, the Defence proposes an alternative solution, which is for the Trial Chamber to order the Prosecution to triage and properly organise the documents in its possession and migrate relevant items to a new case record containing all exculpatory evidence and duly-triaged Rule 77 and incriminating evidence, with a maximum number of items that would be manageable within the constraints of these proceedings. This is the only way in which the start date for trial proceedings of 30 November 2026 could fairly be maintained," he added.
Haynes noted that the deadline for the defense team to file its pre-trial brief is October 30, while the start of the trial is on November 30.
Duterte is facing charges of crimes against humanity in connection with the killings in his war on drugs when he was mayor of Davao City and when he was President.

Earlier this month, the ICC Trial Chamber III unanimously decided to keep Duterte detained as it found a likelihood of the former president “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.” —KG, GMA News

articles.title: British climber, 28, dies in fall in northern Spain
articles.summary:
Mountaineer’s body recovered about 20 metres below the summit of Torrecerredo, the highest peak of the Picos de Europa range

A British man has died after falling about 61 metres (200ft)…

blocks.text: A British man has died after falling about 61 metres (200ft) while descending from the summit of a mountain in northern Spain, according to local law enforcement.

The 28-year-old mountaineer fell down a vertical gully on the east side of the Torrecerredo – the highest peak of the Cantabrian mountains – on Thursday afternoon, the Spanish Civil Guard for the Asturias region said.
The mountaineer’s remains were located after a rescue team aboard a helicopter flew over the area, the Civil Guard said.
Two specialists were lowered to retrieve the man’s body and his belongings which had been scattered during the fall.
The incident occurred during the descent, about 20 metres below the Torrecerredo peak, the Civil Guard said.
The mountaineer’s body was transported to La Morgal, a regional sports and aviation facility in Llanera near the Asturian city of Gijon.
A spokesperson for the UK Foreign Office said it had contacted local authorities about the death.
Torrecerredo, which has an elevation of about 2,649 metres, is the highest peak of the Picos de Europa mountain range, which is part of the larger Cantabrian Mountains range.

articles.title: White House leaves CNN off upcoming Trump trip on Air Force One
articles.summary: The White House signalled Friday night that CNN would be left off Air Force One for U.S. President Donald Trump's Saturday trip, the latest media restriction from the administration in an ongoing…

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump boards Air Force One in New York City on Tuesday. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

The White House signalled Friday night that CNN would be left off Air Force One for U.S. President Donald Trump's Saturday trip, the latest media restriction from the administration in an ongoing dispute with First Amendment implications.
Outlet to be replaced by conservative Real America's Voice News
The news organization was replaced by Real America's Voice News, a conservative outlet.

The news came just after journalists from three news outlets that Trump banned last week from the White House grounds — CNN, MS NOW and Politico — returned to the executive complex with TV cameras, laptops and microphones in hand.

A judge temporarily struck down the ban in an overnight ruling early Thursday, but his decision didn't directly address the pool. The networks continued to refrain from covering Trump as part of the pool, even as reporters from all three outlets were allowed back in the White House.
The temporary order from the judge mentioned only the White House grounds and said nothing directly about Air Force One.

items: White House reporters from outlets banned by Trump regain access after hours-long delay

blocks.text: Theodore Boutrous Jr., the news outlets' attorneys, did not immediately respond to requests for comment from The Associated Press on Friday night.

For a while earlier Friday, the U.S. network video pool for the White House was back in operation for the first time since Trump banned the three news outlets in an extraordinary showdown over media access.

At noon on CNN, viewers could see Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping touring the National Archives, along with Melania Trump and Peng Liyuan, Xi's wife. The banner along the bottom of the screen read: "Trump and China's Xi Visit National Archives." It was a routine report from a state visit — but for the fact that CNN had not aired live video of Trump in several days.
"As of now, all systems are go," said a person familiar with the pool, speaking on condition of anonymity because of the fluidity of the situation.

items: White House reporters from outlets banned by Trump regain access after hours-long delay

blocks.text: The pool consists of five major U.S. broadcast outlets that take turns shooting and sharing video. When the White House banned CNN — which belongs to the pool — from White House grounds, along with MS NOW and Politico, the other four pool providers declined to participate in a show of solidarity.

CNN did not comment directly earlier Friday, referring instead to its editorial coverage. But Brian Stelter, the network's media analyst, posted on X that CNN had a pool assignment at the National Archives event and that the White House had approved the network's credentials.

articles.title: White House blocks CNN from Air Force One in latest escalation with news media
articles.summary:
Outlet had been scheduled to fly with Donald Trump to Tennessee for a college football game, network said Friday

The White House has blocked CNN from traveling aboard Air Force One on…

blocks.text: The White House has blocked CNN from traveling aboard Air Force One on Saturday, impeding its TV press pool duties in the latest escalation of the administration’s battle with the news media.

CNN had been scheduled to fly with Donald Trump to Tennessee for a college football game, the network said on Friday. The White House confirmed CNN’s exclusion when it did not list the network on guidance sent to the press corps regarding Trump’s schedule for Saturday.
CNN’s exclusion from Air Force One was first reported by the Washington Post. The White House did not immediately return the Guardian’s request for comment.
The incident comes a week after Trump, a vocal critic of what he deems the “fake news media”, revoked White House access for CNN, MS Now and Politico, citing unfavorable reports about his presidency.
“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES,” Trump wrote then on Truth Social, vowing that similar action would be taken against other outlets.
The extraordinary move prompted swift backlash from the White House press pool, who suspended their video coverage of Trump in protest.

The press pool is a rotating group of journalists charged with covering presidential travel and disseminating written and multimedia reports to news outlets that may not be present at a given White House event. Since the beginning of Trump’s second administration in 2025, the White House has decided which outlets cover the president via the pool each day, a task previously coordinated by the White House Correspondents’ Association.

In a joint statement Monday, the White House television pool said: “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”
In a subsequent lawsuit, CNN, MS Now and Politico argued the White House ban was a violation of the first amendment.
Meanwhile, the Department of Justice’s attorneys suggested the ban was in the interest of national security, pointing at media reports involving “sensitive” and “classified” information.
The US district judge Timothy Kelly sided with the outlets, ordering the Trump administration to restore their White House access.
CNN, MS Now and Politico’s journalists sought to enter the White House on Thursday morning, but were not granted entry until midday.
Hours later, CNN’s editorial team along with an MS Now reporter were blocked from covering the state dinner commemorating Chinese president Xi Jinping’s visit.

articles.title: ‘Queenie’ keeps strength, may become typhoon as it exits PAR Sunday
articles.summary: Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (international name: Surigae) maintained its strength as it decelerated while moving over the Philippine Sea, PAGASA said Saturday morning.

blocks.text: September 26, 2026 | 9:20am
Satellite rendering shows Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (international name: Surigae) taken as of 4:40 a.m. of Sept. 26, 2026.
PAGASA via Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (international name: Surigae) maintained its strength as it decelerated while moving over the Philippine Sea, PAGASA said Saturday morning.
In its 5 a.m. bulletin on Saturday, September 26, the state weather bureau said Queenie was carrying maximum sustained winds of 95 kilometers per hour near the center, with gusts of up to 115 kph.
It is moving northwestward at 15 kph.
The center of Queenie was estimated at 600 kilometers east of Itbayat, Batanes.
PAGASA said strong to storm-force winds extend outward up to 280 kilometers from Queenie's center.
Queenie is unlikely to directly affect the country's land areas throughout the forecast period.
Sea conditions
PAGASA said moderate seas of up to 2 meters are expected over the northern seaboard of Batanes in the next 24 hours.
Mariners of motorbancas and similarly sized vessels were advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.
Other coastal waters are expected to have wave heights of less than 2 meters.
Track, intensity
Queenie will continue decelerating while moving north northwestward in the next 12 hours before turning north northeastward by Sunday morning, September 27.
On the forecast track, the center of Queenie is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility between Sunday afternoon and evening.
Outside the PAR, Queenie will accelerate northeastward toward the sea east of mainland Japan.
PAGASA said Queenie will likely intensify into a typhoon by Saturday evening or Sunday and strengthen further while moving over the sea south of the Okinawa Islands.
After reaching peak intensity, Queenie is expected to weaken by Monday, September 28.

articles.title: Trump uses contested power to cut nearly $1B US in Congress-approved spending
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is cancelling nearly $1 billion US in spending approved by Congress, the White House announced on Friday, using a rare and contested power to axe funding for immigrant…

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump's Office of Management and Budget described the funding cut as focused on 'the most harmful government spending.' (Manuel Balce Ceneta/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

U.S. President Donald Trump is cancelling nearly $1 billion US in spending approved by Congress, the White House announced on Friday, using a rare and contested power to axe funding for immigrant services and diversity-focused initiatives.
U.S. president's 'pocket rescission' move slammed as illegal; most cuts focused on services for immigrants
Trump's Office of Management and Budget (OMB) described the funding cut as focused on "the most harmful government spending."

Most of the cuts are focused on services for immigrants, including non-profits that serve refugees and unaccompanied minors accused of being in the country illegally. The administration says the funds are no longer necessary because illegal border crossings have diminished considerably.
A White House news release announcing the funding cuts notes some of the organizations are led by people who worked in the administration of former president Barack Obama, a Democrat.
Trump's move was condemned by Sen. Susan Collins, a Republican in a tough re-election campaign and chair of the Senate Committee on Appropriations.

items: Carney's comments over possibility of U.S. invasion reveal how contingency plans are always in place
Trump's top trade envoy says U.S. 'comfortable' with state of relationship with Canada

blocks.text: Collins said in a statement that the action came without warning or consultation. She also said she would work to address with colleagues "these illegal actions."
"… It is a usurpation of Congress's appropriations powers," Collins said. "OMB is an agency of the executive branch. It does not get to decide which programs are worth funding."
'Pocket rescission' manoeuvre

Typically, Congress can review the president's proposed spending cuts before they take effect. But Trump made that all but impossible by announcing them with just five days left in the federal fiscal year.
The Government Accountability Office — the independent, non-partisan watchdog agency that works for Congress — says the manoeuvre, known as a "pocket rescission," is illegal.
Judge blocks Trump’s White House media ban
Collins called it the latest attempt by OMB to "undermine Congress's constitutional power of the purse."

A year ago, Trump issued a pocket rescission for the first time in 50 years by blocking $4.9 billion US in congressionally approved foreign aid. The U.S. Supreme Court declined to block those rescissions, saying Trump's authority over foreign affairs weighed heavily in its decision. This year, Trump is targeting domestic spending.
The use of a pocket rescission fits a broader pattern by the Trump administration to exact greater control over the U.S. government, eroding the power of Congress.

The administration has also fired federal workers, imposed a historic increase in tariffs, and started the war in Iran without going through Congress, putting the burden on the judicial branch to determine the limits of presidential power.

articles.title: Sara Duterte says she does not know Gracioso, has not received money from him
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday said she does not know Rodulfo Gracioso Jr, the former policeman who served as a security officer for former Speaker Lord Allan Velasco, and neither did she…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 8:46am

Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday said she does not know Rodulfo Gracioso Jr, the former policeman who served as a security officer for former Speaker Lord Allan Velasco, and neither did she receive money from him.
"Mga kababayan, I do not know Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., nor have I ever received any money from him," Duterte said in a statement.
"My lawyers are awaiting an official copy of the Gracioso affidavit from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) so they can begin working on the cases to be filed against him," she added.
"Once we are done dismantling the lies contained in his testimony, it will end up in the trash bin—just like the one from Ramil Madriaga," Duterte said.
The vice president said Gracioso's allegation is "another media stunt," adding that the Marcos administration is bent on bringing her down.

"This is nothing more than another media stunt, an attempt to breathe life into a faltering impeachment case. The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical," she said.
"The people want Marcos to take a public drug test. The people want Marcos to answer for the flood control scandal. The people want change," Duterte said.
"No amount of political maneuvering, propaganda, or manufactured distractions can ultimately silence the Filipino people. Shukran," she added.

The NBI is investigating the claims of Gracioso, who said that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte on Velasco’s instructions. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Free the Strip! Melburnians fight back against outlawing of much-loved picnic spot
articles.summary:
A council ban on drinking on the median strip in Canning Street, Carlton, sparks a peaceful protest featuring punch bowls, chips and laughter

  • Get our

blocks.text: It looked like a typical spring evening on Melbourne’s Canning Street when a few dozen picnickers gathered on the grassy median strip on Friday, with drinks in hand.

People in one group who’d come with a full alfresco setting chattered as they ladled punch out of a glass bowl on a wooden table, set with a tablecloth and yellow flowers in a vase. Others sat on picnic blankets, passing around bags of chips.

What set this gathering apart was that it was actually against the rules, given the new ban against drinking on the strip. And the picnic had been organised in protest, part of a political saga that is unfolding on one of inner Melbourne’s most beloved streets.

blocks.caption: Protesters on Melbourne’s Canning Street. The median strip, beloved as a social spot, has become a political talking point after drinking on the grass was banned. Photograph: Catie McLeod

blocks.text: It began on Monday, when a local bar and bottle shop, the Wine Corner Store, announced on Instagram that, “due to a few unrelenting miserable neighbours who have been non-stop complaining to the council”, consuming alcohol had been outlawed on the median strips on Drummond, Rathdowne and Canning Streets in Carlton North.

The council was reverting to a former classification of the median strips – which are much wider than a typical nature strip – with the effect that they are no longer treated as park spaces. The council said residents had complained about noise, rubbish and unsafe behaviour.

The community fought back to keep a tradition that has endured for many years. While the council ban followed an initial 29-signature petition that a resident submitted in August, a counter petition calling on council to revoke the ban gathered more than 7,707 signatures in just a few days.
The protest drinks on Friday were civilised.

Amid the uproar – and with people loosely uniting under a banner of Free the Strip! – Adam Pulford, the Greens candidate for the seat of Brunswick at the state election, had posted an invitation on social media for people to join him for a peaceful protest.

blocks.caption: ‘We need to be building community spaces and not getting rid of them,’ one protesters says. Photograph: Catie McLeod

blocks.text: People milled around, chatting and offering each other drinks and nibbles, talking about the importance of preserving places for building connections outside work and home.

“We need to be building community spaces and not getting rid of them,” said Sam Drummond, who attended the gathering. “Particularly post-Covid, there are very few spaces where people can come together and meet in public, in person.”

Others on the strip on Friday had heeded a call from a Canning Street resident, Rachel Richmond, to gather for the same purpose. As the groups coalesced, Richmond said it was “the most civilised act of civil disobedience I’ve ever participated in”.

“This might seem like a very ridiculously middle class thing to protest,” she said. “I mean, it’s literal champagne socialism but honestly, sitting underneath it is an issue about public space and public enjoyment of space.”
The only disorderly incident the Guardian witnessed on the median strip on Friday was a minor skirmish between a chihuahua and a labrador, both on leads.

However, local councillor Edward Crosling, who represents the Carlton North ward, said there had been “genuine amenity concerns”, especially from people living around the Wine Corner Store, and he believed it was unfair the council had been portrayed in a negative way.

Nevertheless, Crosling said council staff had gone too far in banning drinking outright. “There are some people that have been behaving not fantastically but the majority of people are just having a picnic,” he said.

Crosling said he was working with the council staff to prepare a motion for their next meeting in October, which he anticipated would re-classify the median as open space, and look at “particular” measures to address concerns surrounding the Wine Corner Store.
The venue’s owner, Steve Misfud-Ellul, told Australian Associated Press his business had wrongly copped the blame for large groups choosing to stop on the grass near the wine bar.

“We simply sell retail drinks to people and they choose to stop where they stop,” he said. “Ninety-nine per cent of the time it’s people sitting, picnicking on a patch of grass, with the loudest noise being laughing.”
Misfud-Ellul also stressed the council was not to blame.
“The council actually were fantastic and they acted on every complaint; they came through, they check and they saw there was no problem,” he said.

Despite the councillors pledging to fix the problem, the premier, Ben Carroll, waded in on Friday, sharing a post on social media that said: “Consider this unbanned. Because if council doesn’t reverse it, we will reverse it for them”.
Australian Associated Press contributed to this report

articles.title: Mary Jane Veloso reunites with family after being freed from prison
articles.summary: Former overseas Filipino worker Mary Jane Veloso had an emotional reunion with her family early Saturday after being freed from prison.

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 8:12am Updated September 26, 2026 8:16am
Former overseas Filipino worker Mary Jane Veloso had an emotional reunion with her family early Saturday after being freed from prison.
Mary Jane's family members were fetched from Nueva Ecija and brought to Correctional Institution for Women (CIW) in Mandaluyong City to meet her.
Seen on board the coaster upon arrival at CIW were Mary Jane's parents Caesar and Celia Veloso, and her children, according to a report by Gabriel Gonzales of GMA News.
— GMA News (@gmanews) September 25, 2026

Mary Jane, wearing a white T-shirt and pants and with her hair in a ponytail, was already at the CIW gate with Bureau of Corrections personnel when her family arrived, as seen in a video taken by Olan Bola of Super Radyo dzBB.

JUST IN: Mga kaanak ni Mary Jane Veloso, dumating na sa Correctional Institution for Women sa Mandaluyong City mula Nueva Ecija para siya ay sunduin, matapos makalaya makaraang bigyan ng absolute pardon ni Pres. Bongbong Marcos. | via @olanbola pic.twitter.com/pu29WFPovK— DZBB Super Radyo (@dzbb) September 25, 2026
Mary Jane's parents cried upon meeting her at CIW, according to a report by Jamie Santos of GMA News.
In the coaster with her parents, Mary Jane said she could not believe that she was freed after President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. granted her absolute pardon.
"Ako rin, hindi makapaniwala. Hindi ako makapaniwala. Hindi ako makapaniwala. Pero mabait ang Lord. Mabait ang Panginoon," Mary Jane said while hugging and kissing her mother Celia.
(Me too, I can't believe it. I can't believe it. I can't believe it. But the Lord is kind. God is good.)
"'Di ako makapaniwala talaga, anak. Dito ka na sa tabi ko ngayon," Celia said.
(I still can't believe it, my daughter. You are beside me now.)
"Sumasakit ulo ko, 'Nay. 'Wag ka umiyak," Mary Jane said.
(My head is aching, Mother. Don't cry.)
"Ako na mag-aalaga sa 'yo ngayon. Masakit ang ulo mo," her mother said.
(I'll be the one to take care of you now. Your head is aching.)
"Hindi, ako nga mag-aalaga sa inyo eh. Kaya nga ako umuwi eh," Mary Jane said.
(No, I'll be the one to take care of you. That's why I went home.)
"Eh ako, ala nang sakit. Ikaw, masakit ang ulo mo. Alagaan kita," Celia said.
(But I don't have any illness anymore. You have a headache. I'll take care of you.)
"'Pag nakakain na ako ng ano, ng bituka ng manok. Ihaw-ihaw," Mary Jane laughed.
(After I eat chicken intestines. Grilled.)
"Oo, pagluluto kita," her mother said.
(Yes, I will cook for you.)

Marcos on Friday said he already signed on Thursday the document which says he is granting Mary Jane absolute pardon, paving the way for her release from Philippine prison after once languishing on death row in Indonesia over drug charges.
LOOK: Absolute pardon for Mary Jane Veloso signed by Marcos

Mary Jane was arrested on April 25, 2010, at Adisutjipto International Airport in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, after authorities found 2.6 kilograms of heroin in her luggage. She was sentenced to death by an Indonesian court on October 11, 2010.
She has consistently maintained her innocence, saying she was unknowingly used as a drug courier after being given a suitcase by her recruiters.
Her execution was halted in April 2015 after the Philippine government appealed to Indonesian authorities to allow her to testify against her alleged recruiters.

In December 2024, Indonesia agreed to transfer Mary Jane to Philippine custody following years of diplomatic negotiations. She arrived in the Philippines on December 18, 2024, and was transferred to CIW to serve the remainder of her sentence under Philippine jurisdiction.
Mary Jane was formally released from CIW on Friday after the necessary procedures were completed. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Are Ethiopians marching back to war in Tigray?
articles.summary: Exploring the issues behind the escalation of tensions between the TPLF and the national army.

blocks.text: Are Ethiopians marching back to war in Tigray?
Image source, Reuters
Tigrayan forces have been patrolling the streets of Tigray's capital, Mekelle, this week
ByLucy Fleming and BBC Africa
Fighting has erupted in Ethiopia's northern region of Tigray between regional forces and the national army.
Tigray residents, who have been trying to recover from a brutal two-year war that ended in 2022, fear a return to full-scale conflict.
There are reports of panic buying - and now internet and call services have been disrupted.
This means people cannot get access to their money via digital apps in what has become a largely cashless society after ATMs stopped working several months ago.
Why has fighting broken out now?
It follows more than six months of worsening relations between the government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that runs Tigray.

The African Union (AU) brokered a peace deal, known as the Pretoria Agreement, between the two sides, ending the war nearly four years ago - but several issues have remained unresolved that have inflamed tensions.
This year, both sides have been trading blame while troops have mobilised amid pockets of fighting.
This week, major clashes erupted in Tigray and quickly spread into the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions. The two sides disagree over who started the latest escalation.
The TPLF says it was responding to a federal offensive, including drone strikes, while the government says Tigrayan forces attacked first after seizing control of airports in Tigray.
For much of Tigray's modern political history, it has been governed by the TPLF, which first emerged as an armed movement in the 1970s fighting Ethiopia's military government.

It became a major force in the overthrow of the Marxist regime in 1991 and went on to become the most powerful component of the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF), the coalition that governed the ethnically diverse country for nearly three decades.
At times this proved contentious as some felt the TPLF held too much sway as Tigrayans only make up around 6% of Ethiopia's population.
When Abiy Ahmed became prime minister in 2018, he replaced the EPRDF with the Prosperity Party, significantly watering down the TPLF's influence.
Relations between Addis Ababa and the TPLF rapidly deteriorated until war erupted in 2020 in what was one of the most deadly conflicts this century.
The AU mediator estimated some 600,000 people died during the war, which totally cut off Tigray from the outside world and drove the region to the precipice of famine.
An uneasy truce was agreed in November 2022.
Why has the peace deal faltered?
There are four key issues - and two concern the fertile area of western Tigray.
The TPLF lost control of this territory in the early days of the war to Amhara, a region which neighbours Tigray to the west and whose fighters had fought on the side of the Ethiopian army.
Many people in Amhara believe the territory of western Tigray should never have been incorporated into Tigray when regional boundaries were redrawn after the military regime was ousted in 1991.
When its fighters seized control during the recent civil war, hundreds of thousands of ethnic Tigrayan people fled and are now living in homeless camps in Tigray and in the capital, Addis Ababa.
The TPLF wants western Tigray back and for those displaced from the territory to return. The government says the future of the territory needs to be decided by a referendum.

blocks.caption: Image caption, People have been reportedly rushing to buy food, panicking that a full-blown war will start

blocks.text: People have been reportedly rushing to buy food, panicking that a full-blown war will start
For the government, a major matter of contention has been disarmament. It says the TPLF has only handed over old weaponry to the AU and has been hiding its arms.
The two sides have also been at loggerheads over how Tigray should be governed. Under the terms of the deal, an interim administration was appointed by Abiy.

But attempts by the prime minister to influence affairs caused disputes within the TPLF itself and just before the general election in May, which was not held in Tigray because of the security situation, it restored its pre-war administration, disbanding the one set up by Abiy.
This has meant that civil servants are longer being paid and other services have been seizing up, worsening economic conditions.
Who is backing the TPLF?
A major development has seen the TPLF, once politically isolated inside Ethiopia, gain several key allies.

Earlier in September, it joined six other armed movements in forming what is called the Alliance for Survival, which includes those actively fighting the government like Amhara's Fano militia and the Oromo Liberation Army.
Members of the new alliance have different grievances, but they do share one objective: they want to remove Abiy's government from power.

blocks.caption: BBC map of Ethiopia showing the northern states of Tigray, Amhara and Afar. The regional capital of Mekelle is labelled in Tigray and the national capital Addis Ababa is also located near the centre of the country and just outside the three northern states. Eritrea is shown to the north, borderin…

blocks.text: So while the TPLF and Fano forces were on opposite sides during the civil war - and still disagree over the fate of western Tigray - they have temporarily put some of their differences aside.
TPLF officials say they do not want to repeat the situation of 2020, when they felt surrounded and isolated.
Yet analysts caution the alliance may become difficult to maintain because its members ultimately have very different interests.
What is the government's position?
As well as blaming the TPLF for starting the recent fighting, it has criticised the new alliance, portraying it as an attempt to destabilise the country.
It has also accused Eritrea of supporting armed groups inside Ethiopia, something Asmara denies.
During the recent civil war, Eritrea fought alongside Ethiopian troops but the two neighbours, which have long had a volatile relationship, have again fallen out.
Their disagreement centres on the Red Sea and its ports.

Ethiopia, the world's most populous landlocked nation, lost access to them when Eritrea seceded in 1993. Recently Prime Minister Abiy has been pushing for ownership of Eritrea's southern port of Assab - about 60km (37 miles) from the border - and hinted at taking it by force.
What do we know about the bombing in Tigray?
Reports indicate that federal forces have been using drones and other military operations against Tigrayan forces.

The government's stated justification is that it is responding to attacks and trying to defend federal positions and territory. However, the circumstances surrounding individual strikes are difficult to independently verify.
Residents in one recently targeted town told the BBC the drones had hit two schools, which local officials said had been used by Ethiopian troops as military bases during the war.
This suggests Addis Ababa may believe they are again being used for a military purpose - by Tigrayan forces.
The attacks have come amid reports that the TPLF has been forcibly recruiting young men to join its ranks.
What is being done to stop the fighting?
The main diplomatic effort is being led by the AU, which has called for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a return to direct talks.
It has asked former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, the AU's special Horn of Africa envoy, to engage the parties urgently.
The UN has made a similar appeal, warning against a wider and more devastating conflict.
The regional organisation Igad has also called for fighting to stop and dialogue to resume.
The difficulty is that trust between Addis Ababa and Tigray is extremely low, while the formation of the new armed alliance has made the situation more complicated.
Could the fighting spread?
Tigray capital "out of cash" as fighting escalates
Yes, there is a significant risk of wider conflict inside Ethiopia.
The fighting has already moved to areas over and along Tigray's borders, while the government is simultaneously dealing with armed conflicts in other regions, particularly Amhara and Oromia.
The new alliance potentially connects several of these conflicts politically and militarily.
There is also a fear that Eritrea could be drawn in again - this time against the government.
The two aggressors in Sudan's civil war are also on opposite sides when it comes to allegiances in Tigray, potentially complicating matters.
The AU has specifically urged all neighbouring countries not to take actions that could further escalate the crisis.
